name: growth-charts
title: Growth charts
description: WHO (0–24 months) and CDC (2–20 years) growth charts for the patient’s weights and heights, with percentiles and z-scores.
prompt:
Build a GROWTH CHARTS report for one pediatric patient.

INPUTS
- patientId (id, required): the patient.
- encounterId (id, optional): this visit's encounter; its measurements are highlighted.
- visitDate (date, optional): this visit's date; ages and the opening chart set are based on it.
No date range: use the patient's whole history.

DATA
Fetch the patient's Ottehr visits (Appointments tagged OTTEHR-IP/OTTEHR-TM with their Encounters and the Patient) and the patient's vital-sign Observations (vital tags), keeping only the fields the report reads. From each visit take the last weight (kg) and last height (cm) recorded. Calculate BMI from that visit's weight and height (weight ÷ height²), as growth charts conventionally do. Age = days from the date of birth to the measurement's calendar day (in the viewer's time zone) ÷ 30.4375, in months. Skip the section if the patient has no full date of birth or a sex other than male/female.

REFERENCE DATA
Use the official LMS tables only, embedded in the report and generated by script from the source files, never typed by hand:
- WHO Child Growth Standards, birth to 24 months, monthly: weight-for-age, length-for-age, weight-for-length (by length in cm).
- CDC 2000 growth charts, 2 to 20 years, at CDC's half-month ages: weight-for-age, stature-for-age, BMI-for-age.
Interpolate L, M and S linearly between table rows. z = ((value ÷ M)^L − 1) ÷ (L·S), or ln(value ÷ M) ÷ S when L = 0. Percentile = normal CDF of z. For WHO weight-based indicators, use WHO's restricted z-score beyond ±3. Values outside a table's range get no percentile.

IMPLAUSIBLE VALUES
Flag rather than plot as normal: a unit other than kg/cm or a missing value; WHO z below −6 or above +5 for weight-for-age, beyond ±6 for length, beyond ±5 for weight-for-length; CDC modified z for weight below −5 or above +8, stature below −5 or above +4, BMI below −4 or above +8. Show flagged points as a red ✕ (or a red arrow at the edge when off the chart), keep them off the line, and list them with ⚠. A BMI or weight-for-length value built from a flagged measurement is flagged too.

LAYOUT
- One short title line: sex · standard and age span · percentile set · age at this visit, e.g. "Girls · CDC, 2–20 years · percentiles 3rd–97th · age at this visit: 19 y 4 mo".
- A switch drawn as small tabs, "Birth to 24 months (WHO)" | "2 to 20 years (CDC)". It opens on the set that matches the age at this visit.
- Three chart cards per set, each titled by its measure only (e.g. "Weight-for-age"):
  WHO: weight-for-age, length-for-age, weight-for-length; CDC: weight-for-age, stature-for-age, BMI-for-age.

CHARTS (plain SVG, styled like an EHR growth chart)
- Percentile curves: WHO 2/5/10/25/50/75/90/95/98, CDC 3/5/10/25/50/75/90/95/97, each labelled at its right end, the 50th emphasised, light grid, axes with units (age in months under 2, years from 2; length in cm for weight-for-length).
- Curves in a soft pink tint for girls or blue for boys, matched to the EHR palette.
- The patient's measurements as navy points joined by a thin line; this visit's point larger and outlined in EHR blue.
- Hover: a tooltip beside the point (not over the line) showing date · age · value · percentile, e.g. "08/10/2026 · 19 y 4 mo · 73 kg · 88th percentile", and the matching table row highlighted (hovering a row highlights its point).

TABLES (one under each chart)
- Columns: Date, Age, Value (weight at length for weight-for-length), Percentile, z.
- Newest 10 rows first, with a "Show all (N)" link; a note above the table when some measurements fall outside the chart's age or length range.
- Right padding so the z column is never cut off.

FORMATS
- Dates as MM/dd/yyyy. Ages in clinical style: days for newborns ("3 d"), months under 2 years ("12 mo"), then years and months ("4 y 6 mo").
- Percentiles as ordinals ("88th"), "<1st" and ">99th" at the extremes.

DO NOT SHOW
- A patient block (name, date of birth, sex): the EHR header already shows them.
- Any methods or explanatory text (sources, formulas, matching rules): this is a vetted report.
- A head-circumference chart: Ottehr doesn't record head circumference.
